record.paper_title: Open Questions in Charm Decays Deserving an Answer
record.original_question: Is the lifetime ratio tau(D_s)/tau(D^0) equal to 1 up to very small corrections, or does it differ at the approximately 1% level because weak-annihilation contributions and SU(3) flavor breaking have a measurable impact on charm decays?

evidence.quote: Measuring the ratio τ (Ds)/τ (D0 ) with ∼ 1% precision would provide us with a rather sensitive gauge for the impact of ‘weak annihilation’ (WA) in charm decays and for the weight of SU(3)F l breaking.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\tau(D^0)$ and $\tau(D_s)$ denote the total lifetimes of the neutral charm meson $D^0$ (quark content $c\bar u$) and the strange-charmed meson $D_s^+$ (quark content $c\bar s$), respectively. In the heavy-quark expansion for inclusive nonleptonic decays of charm hadrons, the leading contribution is universal and predicts equal lifetimes, while subleading effects — in particular weak-annihilation (WA) diagrams (in which the valence quark and antiquark of the meson annihilate through a $W$ exchange) and breaking of $SU(3)$ flavor symmetry between $u$ and $s$ quarks — generate a difference between $\tau(D_s)$ and $\tau(D^0)$.

Determine the value of the ratio
$$ R \;=\; \frac{\tau(D_s)}{\tau(D^0)} $$
to roughly $1\%$ precision and decide between the following two qualitative scenarios:
(i) $R = 1$ up to very small corrections (i.e. WA and $SU(3)$-breaking effects are negligible in charm decays), or
(ii) $R$ deviates from $1$ at approximately the $1\%$ level or more, indicating a measurable impact of weak annihilation and $SU(3)$ flavor breaking on inclusive charm decay widths.
artifact.status_search_result: Experimental measurements (E791, CLEO, SELEX, and subsequent experiments compiled by the PDG) firmly establish that τ(Ds)/τ(D0) differs from unity well beyond the 1% level. Current world averages give a ratio of roughly 1.2, many standard deviations above 1, demonstrating that weak-annihilation contributions and SU(3) flavor breaking have a clearly measurable impact on charm decays. Thus scenario (ii) is realized.

status_evidence.title: Measurement of the Ds± lifetime (SELEX)
status_evidence.snippet: τDs±/τD0 = 1.145 ± 0.049, combined with E791 (1.254 ± 0.041) and CLEO (1.190 ± 0.042), averaging 7.4σ from unity.
status_evidence.claim: The measured ratio τ(Ds)/τ(D0) differs from 1 at high significance, much more than 1%.

status_evidence.title: Particle Data Group listings
status_evidence.snippet: PDG world-average lifetimes τ(D0) ≈ 410 fs and τ(Ds) ≈ 504 fs.
status_evidence.claim: Current world averages give τ(Ds)/τ(D0) ≈ 1.2, confirming a large deviation from unity.
